publicReleaseNotes: Lamp 1.7.0 adds page data export and restore in the app: Settings → Export page data downloads everything a status page holds as one JSON file (lamp-page-data, version 1): page settings and logo, components with their status history, incidents with every update, draft, internal note and post-incident report, maintenance with notices, subscribers with their channel, components and consent state, and reference numbers. Restore page data checks the file first and restores it all or nothing into a new, empty Lamp, local or hosted, without emailing anyone. Hosted backups and restores need only Node, git and rer (node scripts/export.mjs --remote and node scripts/setup.mjs --restore-from read the deployment's private input file), and a restore no longer needs the setup token. Deploy to Cloudflare is one guided page, and rer deploy --dry-run names each missing input with the step that explains it. A redeploy also keeps OIDC_TRANSACTION_SECRET, so identity-provider sign-ins in progress survive it; rer deploy --rotate-secret NAME replaces a secret on purpose. Sorry subscribers held for cutover and never released are deleted with their addresses 30 days after the reviewed dry run, and Cutover shows that date. The public page also serves RSS beside Atom, per-component feeds and status and uptime badges, /badge.svg and a Shields /badge.json, Statuspage's public API at /api/v2/ (keeping imported Statuspage IDs) and a native paginated API at /api/public/v1/, all read from the published snapshot without internal components, operator names, notes or subscriber data; Settings builds banner, floating notice and status-dot embeds for listed origins. The checkout pins rer 0.2.42. Product screenshot: .github/assets/release/lamp-1.7.0-status-page-1440.png (a business's public status page at 1440 pixels: grouped components with 90-day uptime, an incident in progress with its latest update, and the subscribe form).

MOVE-006.summary: Sorry subscribers held for cutover and neither released nor undone are deleted with their addresses 30 days after the reviewed dry run; Cutover states that date.
MOVE-006.was: Cutover preview: Settings → Cutover is available after a dry run and for saved imports. It shows up to the first 25 old incident and maintenance addresses with proposed or surviving native permalinks, unavailable addresses and source-host limits, source feed answers, unsupported JSON/RSS/widget consumers, and eligible invitations with their original expiry deadline. Once the owner selects a public origin, each Opens check uses a credentialless browser request that follows the redirect and verifies the final native address and successful HTML response; failures remain explicit. The ordered guide covers import, preview, explicit invitations, hostname/custom-domain instructions, rechecking and keeping the source through the confirmation window. It claims neither DNS validation nor inbox delivery. Instatus accepts its documented saved management REST response families with a separate owner acknowledgement that the page and supplied history are published and unrestricted. Known protected or unpublished source records cannot become public. Visual Component parents are groups; audience groups are refused access restrictions. Only confirmed, approved email-only subscriptions with resolved preferences become pending. Exact supplied public-summary incident/maintenance URLs are joined by source ID; missing URLs are not invented. Maintenance ends use explicit timestamps or documented duration minutes under completed/autoEnd semantics, with every update retained silently. Sorry general notices may have no affected component and are carried as resolved informational history without outage claims; cancelled maintenance stays cancelled. Sorry additionally accepts keyless public JSON captures, including paginated components and notices plus full detail for every notice. Partial public previews name uncaptured details and cannot be applied. Subscribers come only from the authenticated API; eligible email rows are held inert without mail or confirmation expiry. After the hostname is live and the watch window closes, an explicit owner invitation action names the configured public origin, records that approval, and releases held rows into pending with a 72-hour window starting at release. Undo cannot recall mail or remove a released row as if it were still unchanged. Sorry numeric notice IDs and supplied notice paths redirect to surviving Lamp incidents or maintenance; `/notices`, `/history` and `/history/YYYY/month` (English month names) redirect to Lamp’s `/history/` while a Sorry import is retained.

migrations.buyerSteps: Back up the installation, then apply pending migrations in order. Stores staged component changes and immutable update snapshots; existing imported history remains unchanged.
Apply after 0027. Adds page wording-check settings with defaults; no owner action is required.

agentUpdateInstructions: Back up data and owner source. Apply the pending component-update and wording-check migrations in order after the backup. Run pnpm install --frozen-lockfile for the rer 0.2.42 pin. Redeploys keep SESSION_SECRET, SUBSCRIBER_TOKEN_SECRET, WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET and now OIDC_TRANSACTION_SECRET as the Worker holds them; a Worker deployed without OIDC_TRANSACTION_SECRET derives a stable one from its kept session secret. Rotate one only on purpose with rer deploy --rotate-secret NAME or LAMP_REPLACE_SECRETS. Sorry subscribers still held for cutover more than 30 days after their reviewed dry run are deleted with their addresses by the first scheduled run after the update: release or undo them first if you mean to keep them. Hosted backups now run with node scripts/export.mjs --remote and restores with node scripts/setup.mjs --restore-from, each with --env-file; neither needs global pnpm, and a restore needs no setup token. Page data files from Settings restore only into a new, empty installation. Run rer verify and pnpm run verify:release from v1.6.0 before adopting.
